Marcus —

Thanks for the quick sync yesterday. We consolidated internal feedback and attached a marked-up MSA. Two points our counsel wants clarified before procurement can sign:

1) Forum fallback: HarborView prefers a two-tier approach — state court in CA for injunctive/provisional measures and arbitration for remaining disputes. Current redline proposes exclusive arbitration with a carve for equitable relief where "immediate injunctive relief may be sought"; counsel is worried that's too narrow and may delay emergency relief.

2) Expedited provisional relief procedure: we proposed a short sequence (notice, 48-hour cure, limited ex parte preservation) and want Redwood to commit to a small list of contacts and response SLAs. Can you confirm Redwood will accept a provisional-access preservation clause and a streamlined notice path?

We've attached the redline (HarborView_MSA_redline.pdf) and a short memo on the provisional relief workflow (expedited_relief_memo.docx).

Marcus / Emily —

Thanks for the materials. I read the redline and memo; below are our legal team's positions and suggested compromise language.

1) Forum / provisional relief carve: We can accept a two-track model only if the MSA states explicitly that (a) arbitration is the exclusive forum for all disputes except "actions seeking injunctive or other equitable relief to prevent irreparable harm," and (b) such actions may be brought in the Superior Court of California (San Mateo County) or a federal court in the Northern District of California. We will add a short sentence clarifying that pursuing equitable relief in court does not waive Redwood's right to compel arbitration on the remaining claims. This addresses your counsel's concerns about timeliness while keeping the arbitration carve limited.

2) Expedited provisional relief procedure: Redwood can agree to an expedited notice-and-response flow: Redwood will acknowledge emergency notices from authorized HarborView counsel within the same business day and provide a written preliminary response within 48 hours. For preservation/access requests that implicate customer data, we'll provide a designated incident liaison and (where necessary) a targeted data export consistent with our security policies; access will be governed by a joint preservation addendum to avoid open-ended rights. We cannot agree to unfettered on-prem access or real-time console credentials.

3) Wording redlines: I've included suggested alternate text (tracked in our internal draft). Key non-starters for Redwood: any language that (i) permits broad forum shopping by allowing HarborView to pick any jurisdiction, (ii) requires immediate full data extraction without a joint preservation process, or (iii) purports to waive Redwood's right to compel arbitration.

Emily — if that is acceptable, we can produce a clean MSA with the compromise wording for HarborView counsel to review. Given your procurement timeline, we should be able to turn a revised draft around by EOD Monday if HarborView confirms the carve language.

Laura Bennett
